segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There were a great many things Mara could have said. She knew all of them. She could have said are you sure. She could have said you needn't. She could have said that the Proprietor would take it to the Board as evidence for stepping the country, and that the Order would take it as evidence for shutting every door but one, and that the Mercury would take it as a headline, and that none of them would ask the girl what she meant by it. She could have said that she had sealed that page so that nobody could ever accuse the girl of borrowing, and not so that a hall full of strangers could read it aloud. She could have said that she was afraid.
segments.instruct: Warm, restrained Australian narration. Preserve each deliberate repeated thought without rushing. Quiet fear beneath factual restraint. Stay in the same adult narrator voice.

segments.text: "I woke," said the Proprietor, "and went to the window, and the lamps went white." He turned his head from the harbour window and looked down the length of the table at Kiva. "I've dreamed it eleven times since. Not often. Not on any night I could choose. Always with a fever, and always near a thing I can't name, and never once since 2611 when I didn't have my hand on this glass. The last was in the ninth month of last year. The 17th. In the evening."
